results.observed: pending 1 -> 0; XACK by a client that never read the entry returned 1
results.meaning: any client able to reach Redis with the group name can mark another consumer's in-flight message as done; the handler may still be running or may fail afterwards, and the message is then lost to recovery (no pending entry left)

results.observed: B claimed 1 entry (owner consumer-B); the stale consumer A then ACKed it: returned 1; pending left 0
results.meaning: XCLAIM moves ownership but gives the previous owner no fence: its late ACK still succeeds and drops B's in-flight entry. There is no fencing token, only a delivery counter, so "exactly one live owner" is not enforced by Redis
the owner is the consumer NAME the client chose (`${group}-${pid}-${uuid8}` in event-store.ts), not an authenticated identity; deliveries is a counter, not a token a handler could present

results.observed: 2 messages published by a third client carried __originInstanceId="victim-instance-uuid" unchallenged
results.meaning: event-store.ts drops any cross-instance message whose __originInstanceId equals its own random uuid (self-echo suppression); the id appears in every message, so a client with publish rights can copy it and make the victim instance ignore chosen events
